# Zoning & Development Analysis: 1601 N Milwaukee Ave

**PIN:** 14313320180000 | **Parcel resolution:** Authoritative (county address records)

---

## 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2** (Community Shopping District, bulk density 2), per the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning system (Ordinance No. 17230). You can verify this on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

The B3 district is the broadest commercial district, designed to accommodate a wide range of retail and service uses, often in larger buildings than found in B1/B2 districts [1]. The "-2" suffix denotes the applicable floor area ratio and density tier — see §17-3-0401 for bulk designations [1].

---

## 2. Ground-Floor Retail with Apartments Above

**Yes — this is permitted by right.** Under [2]:

- **Dwelling Units above the ground floor** in a B3 district: **P** (permitted by-right)
- **Retail/commercial uses** on the ground floor: permitted by-right in B3

So a classic mixed-use configuration — retail or commercial at grade, residential above — is allowed without any special use approval in B3-2 [2].

> ⚠️ **Important caveat:** Ground-floor dwelling units (below the second floor) in B3 districts carry restrictions — see Row 4 of the B3 use table [2]. Pure ground-floor residential is not straightforwardly permitted by right; you should confirm with the Department of Planning and Development.

---

## 3. Bulk & Density Standards

The "-2" density designation controls FAR, height, minimum lot area per unit, and setbacks. The Municipal Code section governing these standards for B districts is **§17-3-0400 et seq.** (Bulk and Density Standards), and the specific table for B3-2 is in **§17-3-0401**. Unfortunately, the full numeric table for B3-2 is not included in the code excerpts provided to me, so I **cannot quote specific FAR, height, or lot-area-per-unit figures with confidence** from this context alone.

What I can confirm:
- The parcel has a **land area of 11,951 sq ft** and a **building footprint supporting ~15,647 sq ft** across **2 stories**, built in **1920** (106 years old).
- Setback rules for B districts generally differ from residential (R) districts — the residential setback rules at [4] (§17-2-0309) apply to R zones, not B3. B district setback standards are governed by **§17-3-0400+**.
- For precise FAR, height limit, minimum lot area per unit, and setback numbers for B3-2, **verify directly** at:
  - The [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning)
  - The Chicago Zoning Ordinance text at **§17-3-0401**
  - Or contact the Department of Planning and Development: (312) 744-5777

**Confidence: Moderate** on the district ID; **Low** on specific bulk numbers — the numeric table was not in the retrieved code chunks.

---

## 4. Overlays & Special Designations

This parcel carries **multiple significant overlays** — each with real development implications:

### 🏛️ Historic / Landmark Designations
- **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** — This parcel is within a City-designated historic district. Exterior alterations typically require review by the Commission on Chicago Landmarks.
- **Individual Landmark Building** — The property is flagged as an **individual Chicago landmark** (known in county survey records as "NOEL STATE BANK," rated **orange** in the Chicago Historic Resources Survey). This is the most significant constraint: demolition or exterior alteration of an individually landmarked building requires **Commission on Chicago Landmarks approval** and, for demolition, likely City Council action.
- **Wicker Park Historic District (National Register)** — The parcel is also within the National Register of Historic Places district. This doesn't create a local approval requirement on its own, but it affects eligibility for federal Historic Tax Credits (20% credit for certified rehabilitations) and triggers Section 106 review for any federally funded/permitted work.

### 🚇 Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)
- **CTA TOD Overlay** — The parcel qualifies for CTA rail TOD benefits under Chicago's Connected Communities Ordinance. The Damen Blue Line station is just **0.07 miles away** (under a 2-minute walk). TOD eligibility allows **density and parking bonuses** near transit.

### 🏠 ADU Eligible Area
- This parcel is in an **ADU Eligible Area**, meaning accessory dwelling units (coach houses, basement units, etc.) may be created subject to the ADU pilot program rules.

### 💰 Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone
- The parcel is in an **ARO zone**. Any residential development of 10+ units triggers affordable unit requirements. The West Town community area already has 20 ARO/affordable housing projects totaling 291 units under this program.

### 🌟 Special Service Area — Wicker Park (SSA)
- The parcel is within the **Wicker Park Special Service Area**. Properties in the SSA pay an additional tax levy that funds enhanced neighborhood services (streetscaping, marketing, etc.). Note the tax breakdown reflects a levy to "City of Chicago Special Service Area 33" of **$2,362.99/year** for this parcel.

### ❌ Not Applicable
- Not in a Planned Development
- Not in a Lakefront Protection Zone
- Not in a Pedestrian Street overlay (on_pedestrian_street: false)
- Not in a PMD (Planned Manufacturing District)
- Not in a Special Flood Hazard Area (flood risk is low)

### ⚠️ Nearby Brownfield
- **Park 512 / Avenue Park** (EPA ID: 110005863100) is a registered brownfield site nearby. Environmental due diligence (Phase I/II ESA) is advisable before any ground disturbance.

---

## 5. Parking Requirements & TOD Reduction

Parking standards for mixed-use B3 development are governed by **§17-10-0207-C** (referenced in the use table at [2]) and the broader off-street parking chapter **§17-10**.

Because this parcel:
1. Is within a **CTA TOD overlay** (Damen Blue Line, 0.07 mi), and
2. Is in a **Walker's Paradise** with a Walk Score of 99/100 and Transit Score of 77/100 (Excellent Transit),

…the Connected Communities Ordinance (effective 2023) provides **significant parking reductions or eliminations** near CTA rail stations. Within a half-mile of a rail station (this parcel is ~370 feet away), parking minimums may be **reduced to zero** for certain uses. The exact reduction depends on use type and project size — confirm the applicable ratio under **§17-10-0207** and the TOD overlay standards.

**To verify:** Contact DPD or review Chicago's TOD overlay regulations directly.

---

## 6. Demolition & New Mixed-Use Construction

**This is where the landmark designation becomes the central constraint.**

### The Core Problem: Individual Landmark Status
The building is flagged as an **individual Chicago landmark** ("Noel State Bank"). Demolition of a Chicago landmark is essentially prohibited without:
1. A **Commission on Chicago Landmarks** hearing
2. Likely **City Council approval** to delist the landmark designation

This is an extremely high bar. Landmark demolition is rare and typically requires demonstrating that preservation is economically infeasible. **Do not assume demolition is feasible** without a detailed legal and landmarks review.

### If Demolition Were Approved (or for Renovation):
Even without demolition, new construction or substantial exterior alteration within the **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** and as an **individually landmarked building** requires:
- **Certificate of Appropriateness** from the Commission on Chicago Landmarks
- Compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation (for National Register purposes, especially if using Historic Tax Credits)
